subject: dwarf crocodile
title: Orange Crocodiles Live in a Pitch-Black Cave and Hunt Falling Bats

scenes.text: These crocodiles are orange, and they hunt in total darkness.
They're African dwarf crocodiles, about five feet long, living deep in the Abanda Caves of Gabon.
They live on heaps of bat droppings. Scientists think the acid in it slowly turns the older ones orange.
And they eat the bats. For years nobody could see how: the crocodiles wouldn't hunt with people watching.
In October 2026, cameras finally caught it. Thousands of bats pour out at dusk, collide, and drop to the floor.
The crocodiles are waiting underneath. Some even leap for them.

description:
In the Abanda Caves of Gabon, a population of African dwarf crocodiles lives in total darkness on mounds of bat guano, and eats the bats.
Footage released in October 2026 for a National Geographic series shows them catching bats for what Live Science calls the first time on film: bats collide in the evening rush, fall to the cave floor and are seized. The crocodiles grow to about 1.5 metres, and the acidic guano is thought to turn older animals orange. The ecologist who has studied them for about 15 years said he had never been able to watch a hunt.
Would you walk into that cave? Comment below.
first_comment: The first time the ecologist entered the cave, about 10,000 bats took off around him. Bats or crocodiles: which would bother you more?
